title: Pattern Picker: Which Pattern Fits?
summary: Interview-style scenarios. Name the pattern the interviewer is fishing for.

questions.q: An ATM must dispense an amount using ₹2000, ₹500 and ₹100 notes, largest first. Each denomination's cassette has a limited count.
questions.explain: Each cassette handler dispenses what it can and passes the remainder to the next one. This is the classic CoR interview question.

questions.q: Users subscribe to a YouTube channel and want a notification on every upload.
questions.explain: One subject, many dynamically registered observers.

questions.q: A coffee shop sells espresso with any combination of milk, syrup and whipped cream, and each add-on changes the price and description.
questions.explain: Wrap the base beverage repeatedly. Each wrapper adds cost and description while keeping the same interface.

questions.q: The system must call a legacy SOAP inventory service whose methods and data types don't match your `InventoryService` interface.
questions.explain: Translate one interface to another without changing either side.

questions.q: An order goes through CREATED → PAID → SHIPPED → DELIVERED, and can be CANCELLED only before shipping.
questions.explain: Lifecycle with legal and illegal transitions. The full State pattern if behaviour differs a lot per state, a transition table if it's mostly guards.

questions.q: A drawing app needs undo/redo for move, resize and delete actions.
questions.explain: Each action becomes an object with execute/undo, kept on two stacks. Memento is the snapshot alternative.

questions.q: A product catalog has categories that contain products *or sub-categories*, and you need the total price of any category.
questions.explain: Tree of leaves and containers behind one interface, with recursive aggregation.

questions.q: Uber needs different driver-matching algorithms: nearest, highest-rated, and a new ML-based one next quarter.
questions.explain: Interchangeable algorithms behind one interface, injected into the matcher.

questions.q: A high-resolution image should only be loaded from disk the first time it's displayed.
questions.explain: The proxy has the same interface as the image and controls when the expensive real object is created.

questions.q: In a chat room, users shouldn't hold references to each other. Messages go through the room, which handles delivery and muting.
questions.explain: A central hub coordinates the peers, which removes the N² coupling.

questions.q: Three report exporters (PDF, CSV, HTML) all do fetch → transform → write header → write rows → write footer. Only the formatting steps differ.
questions.explain: A fixed skeleton with overridable steps. In Go, pass the varying steps as an interface (Strategy).

questions.q: The client must place an order with a single call, but that call has to coordinate inventory, payment, shipping and notification services.
questions.explain: One simplified entry point over a subsystem. Your top-level service in most LLD answers is a facade.
